claims.text: The starting material is the HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
Approximately 4 at% Cr will be introduced into the starting alloy.
Adding approximately 4 at% Cr will form a fine, reticulated Laves-phase network within the BCC matrix of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The Laves-phase network will be evenly dispersed in the BCC matrix.
The Cr-induced second phase will interact with moving dislocations and increase strain hardening.
The precipitate network will delay localized deformation and failure during dynamic loading.
The precipitates will absorb deformation energy.
The precipitates will reduce the rate of adiabatic heating during impact loading.
At approximately 10^3 s^-1, the Cr-modified alloy will have dynamic yield and compressive strengths roughly 10–15% higher than the baseline.
The Cr-modified alloy will exhibit more uniform dynamic deformation and a delayed onset of localization.
The Cr-modified alloy will have a dynamic fracture strain greater than 13.5%.
The Cr-modified alloy will produce lower localized temperature spikes during impact.
The predictions apply to adiabatic high-strain-rate deformation around 10^3 s^-1, such as Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar compression.
Heating effects are pronounced under the proposed approximately 10^3 s^-1 loading conditions.
The extent of improvement is sensitive to processing parameters and exact Cr content.
Matched baseline and Cr-modified specimens will be tested under identical Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar protocols at approximately 10^3 s^-1.

The hypothesis is falsified if the modified alloy lacks a statistically significant improvement of at least about 10% in dynamic strength and uniform deformability together with reduced localized temperature spikes.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as approximately 4 at% Cr, but the formula HfZrTiTa0.53Cr0.04 contains only about 1.12 at% Cr when its coefficients are normalized.

The predicted dynamic fracture strain is compared directly with 13.5% 'under dynamic conditions,' although the 13.5% baseline is explicitly identified as a quasi-static value. A matched dynamic baseline value is not supplied.
